stem:
Nidhi counts the mango trees of one variety in the school orchard on Tuesday morning. A classmate says this count is a population. A population is a group of the same kind of organisms living together in a habitat at a given place and time.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: The count is a population if the trees are the same kind and are counted in that orchard at that time.
The count is a population even if she mixes mango trees with neem trees in the same total.
The count is a population only if she also includes mango trees from every orchard in the neighbourhood.
The count cannot be a population because trees are plants, not animals.

teacher.key_rationale: A population needs the same kind of organism in one habitat at a place and time. Mixing kinds, expanding to every orchard, or excluding plants breaks the definition.
